title: The Černý conjecture
statement: Does every synchronizing automaton with $n$ states have a synchronizing word of length at most $(n-1)^2$?
background: Posed in the 1960s. Known upper bounds are roughly cubic in $n$, so the quadratic bound is unproved in general.

title: Wilf's conjecture
statement: Let $S$ be a numerical semigroup with conductor $c$, embedding dimension $e$, and let $l$ be the number of elements of $S$ below $c$. Is it always true that $c \le e \cdot l$?
background: Proposed by Herbert Wilf in 1978. It is proved in many special cases, but not in general.

title: The finite basis problem for finite semigroups
statement: Is there an algorithm that decides whether a given finite semigroup has a finite basis for its identities?
background: The analogous question for finite algebras in general is known to be undecidable. For finite semigroups it is open.

title: The generalized star-height problem
statement: Does every regular language have generalized star height at most one?
background: Generalized star height allows complementation as well as union, product and star. The question of whether the height is bounded by one has resisted proof or disproof.

title: Decidability of Krohn-Rhodes complexity
statement: Is there an algorithm that computes the Krohn-Rhodes complexity of a given finite semigroup?
background: The complexity is the least number of group levels needed in a decomposition. Decidability is known only for the lowest levels.

title: The word problem for one-relation semigroups
statement: Is the word problem decidable for every semigroup presented by a single defining relation?
background: Adjan solved the case of one-relator monoids whose relation sets a word equal to the identity. The general case is a long-standing open question.

title: The Bras-Amorós conjecture
statement: Let $n_g$ be the number of numerical semigroups of genus $g$. Is it true that $n_{g+2} \ge n_{g+1} + n_g$ for every $g$?
background: The counts grow roughly like the Fibonacci numbers. Asymptotic growth has been established, but the exact inequality for all $g$ is the open part.
